mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day period following any observation of FEDFUNDS below 0.1%, the S&P 500 produces negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in the unemployment rate over the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 5-day period following any 0.3pp increase in UNRATE, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is rising but housing starts (HOUST) are falling, it indicates a supply-side shock in the housing sector that disrupts the broader economy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is rising and HOUST is falling, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following such events.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% annualized), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: In the 60-day period following any monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS>0.5% and CPIAUCSL>2.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payrolls above 200 (thousand persons) indicates robust labor market conditions, which typically lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day period following any monthly payroll increase above 200 (thousand), the S&P 500 produces negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 100 (index, 2017=100) signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 5-day period following any INDPRO reading below 100, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts value above 1,000 (thousands of units) indicates strong demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day period following any housing starts above 1,000, the S&P 500 produces negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) are rising and housing starts (HOUST) are falling, it indicates a shift in consumer spending patterns that weakens the broader economy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS is rising and HOUST is falling, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following such events.
